text:
The two failing gains are both about 0.80× their ideal values: a1 = -1000/132529 ≈ -7.55e-3 would be in spec, but the simulated -6.05e-3 is 0.801× that. a2 = -1000/413589 ≈ -2.42e-3 simulates at -1.94e-3, also 0.80×. The R1 and R2 values land near the centers of their windows if Rf = 1000 Ω, so they look like the original design. A common factor on both paths points to the one element shared by both paths, Rf. Its sensitivity is also the largest in both lists (+24.9%). The bias devices M8 and M6 shift the gains by only about 3–4%, so they are weaker candidates. M5 is near triode, which affects tail-current margin and PSRR more than DC gain.

I haven't confirmed this with a simulation. The netlist shows Rf = 1000 Ω, so a value fault there would need to be checked against the original design. A finite-gain explanation (open-loop gain of about 4) would also produce a common 0.80 factor, but the device operating points imply a much higher DC gain, so I consider that less likely.
